title: Stop experience gain at max level?

posts.author: Krosis
posts.body:
Hey guys, I'm creating a chapter based game where each chapter the level cap for all actors increases. The idea is so the player cannot grind levels to beat the optional challenging content in the chapter, and it will be easier to balance knowing his level, skills acquired and access to equipment.
The problem - actors continue to gain exp after they reach the max level and once the player eventually proceed to the next chapter and the level cap increases - the actor suddenly gains multiple levels from the stored experience, maybe even reaching the cap again.
I thought about creating a parallel common event that checks the actor level and if he reaches certain level it sets his SP-parameter EXP to 0%, but it will be quite chunky event because it has to check for chapter # and set a new cap for each one.
And now imagine that with 20 actors and 6-7 chapters.
Won't having so many parallel events be too demanding on the game's memory?
Am I on the right track?
Perhaps some of you guys can think of a more elegant solution.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Set Level Cap
Is there a plugin that allows a user to set a level cap limit? I want to setup a level cap, so that the player doesn't over level until the area or chapter is cleared.

posts.author: pawsplay
posts.body:
Instead of making an event for the whole party, you could just test the actors, which in a lot of cases is just four actors. If their level = (whatever the max level is for the chapter they are leaving), THEN change their level -1, then change their level +1. Four tests in one event before you go to the next chapter.
For later chapters, just change the level to whatever you are using for that chapter. No reason to write a lot of code.

I don't see why that's a problem. The stated problem is characters gaining multiple levels when a new cap is set. My suggestion makes sure their XP is not above what is needed for their current level. Also, if you simply stop gaining XP, the characters will be at some probably small, but arbitrary, number of XP above the minimum for their level; my suggestion simply caps them at a specific value. I'd rather have consistency.
For complete consistency, the ideal would probably be to set a maximum number of XP, rather than a maximum level. You would then not have to adjust anything; actors won't be a small, arbitrary number of XP into the next level; the player can see that they are no longer accumulating XP after a certain number. Triggering a "stop gaining XP" behavior seems like a kludge to me.

I understand the engine plenty fine, and understand how limited it is if you only use event commands (i.e. the limited set of functions the devs decide to make UI buttons for). Scripting gives you access to all the code and lets you add your own.
Because RPG Maker is a template-based engine, everything is already designed a certain way to be plug and play and beginner-friendly. This includes how level ups work. If you want to break away from the template you have to overwrite the hard-coded function with a plugin like ATT_Turan did.
